analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head text (lines 1-1046) against the patch. Changed lines visible: line 207 swaps autopilotAllowsModel for autopilotServesModel; lines 397 and 434 add transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) calls; a reconcileAutopilotPlacements() call at ~1148 on unload; and edits near 1298-1306 that fall outside the supplied text.

Security-relevant behavior reviewed:
- Weight-hash handling is unchanged. The TOCTOU bracket around container loading (captureWeightHash, finalizeReusableSSDLoad) stays fail-closed for reusable SSD cache: a missing hash disables cache reuse, and a pre/post mismatch aborts the load and unloads. This bears on T-041, T-012 and T-027 and shows no regression.
- The line-207 gate is stricter or equal in intent, since it now requires that the model is actually served. It still keeps the explicit command-owned load exception. I cannot see the definition of autopilotServesModel, so whether it is at least as restrictive as autopilotAllowsModel is unverified.
- The new transitionGenerations.begin calls at 397 and 434 are at points where isLoadingAny and modelsLoading are set. The matching end/finish paths are not visible in the supplied text. A leaked generation could cause availability or staleness issues, but there is no concrete evidence of that. The catch and finish paths at 965-1045 do not show an obvious corresponding end call. It is unknown whether the generation handle is released via defer or in the helper, which is a question for integration.
- Lines 1148-1150 and 1298-1306 are only partially visible, so the reconcileAutopilotPlacements timing and the edits around 1298-1306 were not fully examined.

There is no new data exposure, authorization bypass or plaintext path in the visible code. Remaining questions are the lifecycle of the transitionGenerations .modelLoading entries on all exit paths, including the early returns for managedSuper and nativeLoad, and the semantics of autopilotServesModel.
